Hi Sam/Tara —

Thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff.

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer support assistant to reduce average handle time and deflect tickets.
- Key workloads: short-form chat (<= 512 tokens), multi-turn context, tool calling for knowledge-base lookups.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 generate < 200ms for single-turn (Sam noted target of 150ms for interactive — happy to prioritize).
- Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent low-latency sessions (approx 12 req/s peak).
- Cost: goal to be <= $0.002 per 1k tokens served during POC (target for evaluation).
- Quality: F1 on intent extraction >= 0.85 on your test set; tool-calling accuracy TBD once schema is locked.
- Security/privacy: no PII to be sent to hosted environment; if required we'll use Private deployment or hashed tokens.

POC plan / timeline (proposed):
- By Aug 14: Acme to confirm success criteria and share representative sample prompts + schema for tool calls.
- Week of Aug 17: Kickoff + integration week (SDK install, API route mapping, initial streaming test).
- Week of Aug 24: Validation & evals (latency, throughput, quality checks).
- Sept 3: POC wrap-up and recommendation.

Owners & roles:
- Acme engineering lead: Tara Lee (integration and test data).
- Redwood integration lead: Marissa Cole (program), Technical owner: Dev Patel (implementation).
- Redwood SRE: Sean Gallagher (performance tuning, SLA discussion).

Action items (next steps):
1) Tara: confirm success criteria and share sample prompts + tool schema by Aug 14.
2) Acme infra: provide sandbox credentials (or confirm need for VPC/private deployment).
3) Redwood: share integration checklist + initial SDK snippets (attached).
4) Schedule 60-min kickoff during week of Aug 17 — propose 8/17 or 8/18.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (high-level tasks + sample perm sets).

If this looks good I'll loop in our solutions engineer and send a calendar invite for kickoff.

Best,

Subject: Re: Acme POC - Integration & Success Criteria (next steps)

Looping in a technical sketch of the integration so Acme has concrete steps to validate during the integration week. High-level plan below + test snippets. I attached a short markdown guide (poc_setup_guide.md).

High-level integration steps:
1) SDKs & auth
   - Languages: Python (redwood==0.9.0), Node (npm package @redwood/inference).
   - Auth: API key for sandbox; we can swap to OAuth or short-lived creds for Private deployments.

2) API routes (recommended mapping)
   - POST /v1/generate -> sync generation (JSON request body: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature).
   - POST /v1/stream -> streaming responses via SSE or websocket (supports chunked tokens and partial JSON events).
   - POST /v1/embeddings -> batch embeddings endpoint for offline evaluation.
   - POST /v1/call_tool -> server-side tool call relay (schema-driven) that invokes your KB webhook and returns structured output.

3) Streaming & tool calling details
   - Streaming modes: SSE (EventSource) and WebSocket; SSE preferred for simple browser flows, WebSocket for bi-directional latency-sensitive flows.
   - Partial JSON framing: each data: event contains {"delta": ... , "cursor": ...}. Client should accumulate and apply incremental updates.
   - Tool calling: include a tool_schema in request. When runtime returns a tool invocation, Redwood will POST to your webhook with signature header X-Redwood-Sig.
     - Retry: exponential backoff x3, then surface tool error in the response object.

4) Caching & performance knobs
   - Prefix caching: common prompt prefixes are cached per model variant.
   - KV cache warmup: for multi-turn sessions we recommend persisting the KV cache between requests for the session id.
   - Batching: enable automatic batching for throughput tests; disable for strict latency SLAs.

5) Test & validation
   - Redwood will provide sandbox API keys and a small token budget for performance testing.
   - Provide anonymized test set; we'll run automated latency and quality runs and share results.

Sample Python (streaming) snippet:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED_SANDBOX_KEY")
with client.stream("gpt-redwood-1", prompt="Customer: ...\nAgent:") as s:
    for event in s:
        if event.type == "token":
            print(event.delta, end="")
        elif event.type == "tool_call":
            # handle tool call event
            print("TOOL CALL:", event.payload)
```

Sample curl for tool-calling webhook:
curl -X POST https://acme-kb.internal/call -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"account status 123"}'

Attachments: poc_setup_guide.md (includes SDK install, sample requests, and checklist).

Happy to jump on a deep-dive during kickoff.
